default.text: Madam Deputy Speaker, this Budget is built on the Office for Budget Responsibility’s March forecast, brought up to date for today’s borrowing costs and prices, and on the rules this government set itself. Every figure in it starts from theirs; every choice in it is mine.

cost-of-living.text: Madam Deputy Speaker, this is a Budget for the cost of living. Bills are rising again this winter, and the people who feel that first are the people this Budget is for.

nhs.text: Madam Deputy Speaker, this is a Budget for the health service people rely on: a waiting-time promise kept, and the first steps to a national care service.

defence.text: Madam Deputy Speaker, the first duty of any government is the security of its people: defence on the path our allies expect. This Budget funds that duty.

schools-send.text: Madam Deputy Speaker, this is a Budget for the children the system has let down: special needs provision councils can afford, and schools that can plan.

homes-growth.text: Madam Deputy Speaker, this Budget moves money and power out of Westminster and into every postcode in Britain. It is built on fiscal discipline, and it invests.

families.text: Madam Deputy Speaker, this is a Budget for families: for the children we lifted out of poverty last year, and for the ones we have not yet reached.

safer-streets.text: Madam Deputy Speaker, the first duty of any government is the safety of its people: prisons that hold, and borders that work. This Budget funds that duty.

welfare-bill.text: Madam Deputy Speaker, this is a Budget that faces the welfare bill honestly: what it costs, who it reaches, and what we will change.

openingStarted.text: Madam Deputy Speaker, this Budget makes a start on {priority}. It does not finish the job, and I will not pretend that it does.

forecast.text: On today’s estimate, before any measure in this Budget, we borrow {borrowingThen} in {startYear} and {borrowingTarget} in {targetYear}. {change}

up.text: This Budget adds {amount} to borrowing in {targetYear}.

down.text: This Budget cuts borrowing in {targetYear} by {amount}.

same.text: This Budget leaves borrowing in {targetYear} about where it was.

priority.text: {title}: {options}, {price} in {targetYear}. A priority agreed in Downing Street, and a priority delivered.

cuts.text: Some budgets will get less than planned: {measures}.

welfareCuts.text: We will save on benefits: {measures}. I know who that falls on, and I say so.

broad.text: Everyone contributes: {measures}, raising {yield} in {targetYear}. I know what that means for working people, and I say so.

top.text: Those with the broadest shoulders bear the greatest burden: {measures}, raising {yield} in {targetYear}.

business.text: Business will contribute too: {measures}, raising {yield} in {targetYear}.

motorists.text: Motorists pay a little more: {measures}, raising {yield} in {targetYear}.

base.text: We broaden the base of VAT: {measures}, raising {yield} in {targetYear} on HMRC’s figures for the reliefs we end.

compliance.text: We will collect what is already owed: {measures}, raising {yield} in {targetYear} if the next compliance package yields what the last one did.

giveaways.text: And we cut taxes where we can: {measures}.

lockBreak.text: I will be straight with the House. This Budget does not keep every promise this government made: {promises}. I chose that, and I will answer for it here.

met.text: On today’s estimate, this Budget meets the fiscal rules, with {headroom} of headroom in {targetYear}. The Office for Budget Responsibility publishes its own verdict today. I commend this Budget to the House.

missed.text: On today’s estimate, this Budget misses {missed}. The Office for Budget Responsibility publishes its own verdict today, and I will answer for mine. I commend this Budget to the House.

rulesMissed.text: This government wrote the fiscal rules, and today it breaks them. If it will not keep its own rules, why should anyone lend to it on trust?

promiseBroken.text: They promised the country, in black and white, and they have broken that promise today. Why should anyone believe the next one?

taxUp.text: Another Budget of higher taxes, on top of a tax take the forecasters already call a historic high. No country taxes its way to growth.

borrowingUp.text: They are borrowing more and calling it a plan. Our children will pay the interest on today’s choices.

cuts.text: Today’s Budget cuts what people rely on, on top of the squeeze already in the plans. That is not a plan; it is managed decline.

default.text: A Budget of small steps from a government that promised change. The country deserved more ambition than this.
